newsitem.title: KENYA: Burundi army says 57 villagers killed in fighting.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army says 57 villagers killed in fighting.

text.p: Burundi's army on Wednesday said 57 villagers were killed in fighting between the army and Hutu rebels south of the capital Bujumbura last Thursday.
Army spokesman Isaie Nibizi said the 57 had gathered at a market in the village of Rumonge, 60 kms (40 miles) from the capital, and were killed when the army and rebels opened fire at the same time.
"It seems that those who died were civilians and a team has now been sent to Rumonge to find out exactly what happened there," said Nibizi.
There was no independent confirmation of the number of dead in the incident or of the way in which the villagers died.
Nibizi said the army suffered only light casualties at Rumonge and that casualty figures for the rebels were not available.
"They do not wear uniforms so it is difficult to tell who they are," the spokesman said.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and fighting between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since the killing of Burundi's first elected Hutu president in October 1993.

Regional sanctions imposed last year have failed to push Burundi's Tutsi military leader Major Pierre Buyoya, who seized power last July, into unconditional talks with the rebels of the Hutu majority, who are fighting for a bigger political say.
A regional summit to review sanctions on Burundi had been scheduled for the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha on April 8 but diplomatic sources said it had been postponed indefinitely.
